spec_match.rationale: Runs the same background fetch against a genuinely cross-origin URL (localhost vs 127.0.0.1) with and without Access-Control-Allow-Origin and reads the enforcement difference out of the worker's records — the exact contract Chrome 154 aligns with the Fetch CORS protocol.

interactive.rationale: Two fetch buttons plus Clear drive real background fetches; verified both branches live — the CORS row readable, the plain row failing with 'UnknownError: The response is not available'.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises the same download with the CORS header switched on and off, and both runs land in one comparison table with an interpretation.

edge_cases.rationale: The one-per-gesture/one-in-flight refusal has its own explanatory branch, the how-to-read section covers all four readability outcomes including the backwards one, and the neither-readable case defers to the step evidence.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/6210300985606144 and the Fetch Standard CORS protocol section.

conformance.rationale: The suite's opaque-vs-cors fetch pair mirrors this page's contract and passed, but background-fetch-requires-user-activation reads FAIL on a fresh profile because no service worker registration exists — flagged for a human, not edited.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): trusted CDP clicks 8s apart ran both fetches; worker reported backgroundfetchsuccess for the cors=1 request (200, readable yes) and backgroundfetchfail for the plain one (response not available), summary declared enforcement on; console clean, desktop and mobile screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and emits a cors-comparison assert with corsReadable/plainReadable once both runs are in.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, button colour pairs overridden together, step/verdict colours from accent variables, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: aria-live output, captioned table with scoped headers, text alternatives beside aria-hidden icons, labelled buttons with 44px min-height.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read); URLs truncate/wrap inside the table.

openQuestions.title: Fix the stale :8123 port in the cross-origin explainer
openQuestions.detail: The note hard-codes 'http://localhost:8123 and http://127.0.0.1:8123' while the live origin readout directly above it correctly shows the real server (:3000 locally, the deployed origin in production). The mismatched example port makes the explanation look wrong next to its own evidence; derive the example from location.origin/otherOrigin() like the readout does.

openQuestions.title: Update the detail readout after a single run, not only after both
openQuestions.detail: summarise() returns early until both the with-CORS and without-CORS runs have reported, so after one fetch the aria-live detail still says 'Fetching ... The service worker will report the result' even though its row has already landed. Announce the single-run result ('with-CORS readable — now run the other one') so screen-reader users and the visible readout stay truthful between runs.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/cors-enforcement-for-background-fetch/cross-origin/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp). Trusted CDP Input clicks (which grant user activation) ran both branches for real against http://127.0.0.1:3000 from http://localhost:3000: the Access-Control-Allow-Origin request succeeded and was readable (200/default) while the headerless request ended in backgroundfetchfail with 'UnknownError: The response is not available', and the page concluded 'enforcement is on'. Notably this Chromium 141 build already enforces the record-read path, which the page's outcome-agnostic copy handles honestly. Console clean bar intentional logs; desktop 1280 and mobile 360 DPR3 screenshots read with no overflow; /conformance/ ran 6 pass / 1 fail (the fresh-profile user-activation assertion, flagged separately). Two minor copy/readout follow-ups.
